facts.value: In 1689 James II's troops used Trinity College as a barracks and prison, but the library came through largely unharmed.
facts.quote: the troops of James II had occupied the College as a barracks and prison. A substantial amount of vandalism was inflicted on many of the buildings, but the Library escaped relatively unscathed
facts.check: curl -sL -A 'Mozilla/5.0' 'https://www.tcd.ie/library/exhibitions/choicebooks/newlibrary.php' | perl -0pe 's/<[^>]*>/ /g;s/\s+/ /g' | rg -o -m1 -F 'the Library escaped relatively unscathed'

facts.value: The sandstone on the upper floors of the new library crumbled within decades and was later replaced with granite.
facts.quote: The original pale sandstone masonry on the upper floors of the new Library crumbled within decades, and was eventually replaced with granite

facts.value: The alcoves once held benches and sloping desks for readers. In 1817 the seats and tables were removed to make room for more shelves.
facts.quote: Extra space was gained by removing the seats and reading tables in 1817. Shelves were built in their place
facts.check: curl -sL -A 'Mozilla/5.0' 'https://www.tcd.ie/library/exhibitions/choicebooks/newlibrary.php' | perl -0pe 's/<[^>]*>/ /g;s/\s+/ /g' | rg -o -m1 -F 'removing the seats and reading tables in 1817'

facts.value: Henry George Quin left 110 books with a bookcase for them and orders that their bindings were never to be altered.
facts.quote: bequeathed to Trinity College Library 110 books, a book‐case in which to keep them, and instructions that the bindings were never to be altered

facts.value: The Book of Kells and the Book of Durrow reached the library as a gift from Henry Jones, a pupil of Archbishop Ussher.
facts.quote: the Book of Kells and the Book of Durrow, were presented by Ussher’s pupil, Henry Jones

facts.value: In 1802 around 20,000 books and manuscripts of Hendrik Fagel, chief minister of the Netherlands, were bought for the college.
facts.quote: In 1802 around 20,000 books and manuscripts formerly belonging to bibliophile Hendrik Fagel, chief minister of the Netherlands, were purchased for the College
